purpose: Determine whether the two independent ffn_gate and ffn_up oneDNN GEMMs can profitably overlap on one B70 before modifying the llama.cpp graph executor.
scope: Mechanism-only microbenchmark; no rate from this test is an endpoint or publishable model result.
hardware: Each of the two local Intel Arc Pro B70 cards tested separately; no remote host.
shape: Two independent deterministic f16xf16->f32 oneDNN matmuls with A=[1,8704,5120], B=[1,5120,96], C=[1,8704,96], matching the dominant c96 gate/up shape in r22.
arms: Serial execution of both primitives on one in-order SYCL queue versus concurrent execution on two in-order queues sharing one device/context.
method: Allocate and initialize once; build primitives and user scratchpads outside timing; warm both arms; alternate arm order across timed blocks; wait for all involved queues at each sample boundary; report medians and interquartile ranges.
correctness_gate: Both concurrent outputs must be byte-identical to their corresponding deterministic serial outputs after the timed samples.
advance_rule: Only consider a backend graph-fusion implementation if both local cards pass byte identity and show at least 5% median pair-time reduction. Otherwise close concurrent gate/up execution as unsupported by this evidence.
profile_basis: r22 attributed 42.5-42.7% of oneDNN execution time to the shared gate/up shape and 17.7-17.9% to ffn_down.
